objectives: Students should use cumulative frequency graphs to determine how many data values fall below or above certain thresholds (Maths 6.1)
Students should interpret cumulative frequency graphs to compare distributions (Maths 6.1)
Students should estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range from cumulative frequency graphs (Maths 6.1)

keyConcepts.explanation: A graph that shows the running total of frequencies up to each point in the data set, helping to see how many values fall below a certain threshold.
Median is the middle value, quartiles divide the data into four equal parts, and interquartile range is the difference between the upper and lower quartiles.
Using cumulative frequency graphs to compare shape, spread, and central tendency between different data sets.

steps.title: Introduction to Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: Cumulative frequency graphs show the total number of data points less than or equal to a particular value. They can be used to find how many data values fall below or above certain thresholds, estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range, and compare different data distributions.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Question: Understanding Cumulative Frequencies
steps.content: A cumulative frequency graph is used to find:

questions.question: What can a cumulative frequency graph help you determine?
options: The exact frequency of each individual value
The total number of values less than or equal to a value
The mean of the data set
The range of the data set
questions.answer: The total number of values less than or equal to a value
questions.explanation: Cumulative frequency graphs show the running total of frequencies up to each point, so they help find the total number of data values less than or equal to a certain number.

steps.content: Use the given cumulative frequency graph to estimate the median, lower quartile (Q1), upper quartile (Q3), and interquartile range.

questions.answer: Answer will depend on graph data (e.g., '30')

questions.answer: Answer will depend on graph data (e.g., '55')
